note: Obese/diabetic mice and monkeys predicted the liver-fat and lipid/adiponectin responses every member reproduced; the one published mouse fibrosis prediction (pegbelfermin) failed in FALCON, while efruxifermin and pegozafermin later met the F2-F3 fibrosis endpoint and both missed in cirrhosis.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled). Fc-FGF21(RGE) is AMG 876, later AKR-001/efruxifermin.
engagement.judgement: Model entry; readouts were glucose, lipids and body weight.

engagement.short: Pegozafermin improves lipids, adiponectin in monkeys
engagement.quote: In diabetic monkeys, once-weekly and once-every-2-weeks regimens of subcutaneous pegozafermin provided rapid and robust benefits for an array of metabolic biomarkers, including triglycerides, cholesterol, fasting glucose, glycated hemoglobin, adiponectin, alanine aminotransferase, food intake, and body weight.

dose.judgement: Model entry; no exposure target to carry forward.

dose.quote: We observed a significant decrease in absolute hepatic fat fraction in the group receiving 10 mg pegbelfermin daily (-6·8% vs -1·3%; p=0·0004) and in the group receiving 20 mg pegbelfermin weekly (-5·2% vs -1·3%; p=0·008) compared with the placebo group.

dose.judgement: SYMMETRY (efruxifermin, cirrhosis) missed at 36 weeks but was not abandoned and the 50 mg arm separated at 96 weeks, so it is not a 'reached, failed, abandoned' row; it is recorded under efficacy only.

dose.judgement: Model entry. An in-silico exposure-response model used to choose the phase 2b regimens; its stated target is an average concentration giving near-full HFF effect at 30 mg weekly, with 44 mg every 2 weeks as an effective alternative.
dose.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)

dose.confidence_note: Pairing: ENLIVEN (online 2023-06-24) and the model paper (2023-10-02) do not cite each other at abstract level. Year 2023 is when the model side became public. The model stated no tolerability margin (margin_stated false).
dose.judgement: Not a retrodiction: the model was built from the 2019-2021 phase 1b/2a data and fixed the ENLIVEN regimens before the trial started, even though it was published after the result. Reached, drug worked: both simulated regimens were dosed as planned and improved fibrosis, so same.
dose.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)

efficacy.short: Liver fat fell as mice predicted

efficacy.quote: In obese and diabetic mouse and cynomolgus monkey models, Fc-FGF21(RGE) demonstrated greater efficacies to Fc-FGF21(RG), resulting in larger and more sustained improvements in multiple metabolic parameters.

efficacy.confidence_note: Year from Akero press releases (BALANCED week-12 primary reported in Q1 2020; Q1 2020 results release 2020-05-13); Harrison 2021 sets the status.

efficacy.quote: The primary endpoint-absolute change from baseline in HFF measured as magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction at week 12-was met.

efficacy.judgement: The only member with a published fibrosis-model result is pegbelfermin, and it failed both FALCON trials, so the track is contra. Efruxifermin (HARMONY) and pegozafermin (ENLIVEN) later met the same F2-F3 fibrosis endpoint, but one drug's contra beats another's same on a track and no source shows the FALCON signal was an artefact, so they sit in patient_trials. Both also missed their 36-48-week primary in cirrhosis (SYMMETRY, FALCON 2), which no model addressed.
efficacy.note: FALCON 1 missed its fibrosis/NASH primary endpoint (24-31% vs 14%, no dose response); FALCON 2 in cirrhosis also failed.
efficacy.quote: The FALCON 1 study did not meet its primary endpoint; a ≥1-point decrease in fibrosis score without NASH worsening or NASH improvement without fibrosis worsening assessed via biopsy.

patient_trials.quote: At week 48, 24% to 28% of the pegbelfermin arms had primary endpoint responses vs 31% of the placebo arm (P = .361).
In this phase 2b trial, treatment with pegozafermin led to improvements in fibrosis.
Efruxifermin improved liver fibrosis and resolved NASH over 24 weeks in patients with F2 or F3 fibrosis, with acceptable tolerability, supporting further assessment in phase 3 trials.
In patients with compensated cirrhosis caused by MASH, efruxifermin did not significantly reduce fibrosis at 36 weeks.

efficacy.quote: Simulations showed that the 30 mg q.w. dose approximated the full PD effect; almost all patients would benefit from a greater than or equal to 30% HFF reduction, suggesting fibrosis regression.

The model predicted a surrogate (HFF); ENLIVEN's primary was histological fibrosis improvement, met at 30 mg weekly (22%) and 44 mg every 2 weeks (27%) vs placebo (7%) in the NEJM abstract. The HFF responder proportion in ENLIVEN was not checked, so the magnitude is direction only.

efficacy.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)

Kaufman also notes a later DIO-mouse study found no bone loss with rhFGF21, so the model side is itself contested. FALCON's 48-week BMD (a key safety endpoint) was not retrievable at abstract level.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison in a tier-1 paper, so it strengthens the 2018 entry rather than opening a new status. GI adverse events (diarrhoea, nausea), the class's commonest harm, are unscored: no model stated a prediction and only reduced food intake in monkeys hints at it.
safety.note: Kaufman 2020 sets mouse bone loss beside 12- and 16-week pegbelfermin DXA in T2D and NASH patients: no BMD change.

It reproduced the human absence of bone loss, so retro; a prospective bone comparison would need FALCON's 48-week DXA, which is unreported.

safety.note: Monkeys at clinically matched exposure for a year showed no bone effect, reproducing the no-BMD-change seen in 12-16-week pegbelfermin patients.

safety.judgement: Model entry. The rat was used to test the harms that translated inconsistently for other FGF21 analogues (blood pressure, sympathetic tone, urine volume); it predicted none for efruxifermin and, separately, increased food intake.
safety.model: Sprague Dawley rats, 4- and 26-week efruxifermin toxicology
safety.note: Chronic efruxifermin in rats cut weight gain despite more food intake, lowered urine volume, and left sympathetic and corticosterone markers unchanged.
safety.short: Rats: no sympathetic activation, more food intake
safety.quote: Markers of sympathetic activation, urinary corticosterone and ratio of adrenal-to-body weight were unchanged.

safety.magnitude_basis: systemic blood pressure and cortisol/sympathetic markers: predicted no rise, none seen in T2D (Kaufman 2020) and NASH (Harrison 2021) patients
safety.population: T2D patients up to 70 mg weekly (Kaufman 2020) and NASH F1-F3 patients up to 70 mg weekly for 16 weeks (BALANCED, NCT03976401)

Retro rather than same because the stated comparison was written after both human results were published and the rat run dates are not given; if the 26-week study predates the phase 1 BP data the entry would be same.
safety.judgement: The paper itself sets the rat sympathetic/corticosterone result beside the unchanged blood pressure and salivary cortisol in efruxifermin-treated humans (stated comparison). The rats' increased food intake also matches the increased-appetite adverse event in Kaufman 2020, but the paper does not state that pairing, so it is not scored. Blood pressure is a harm the class had shown with PF-05231023, so the prediction was load-bearing.
safety.model: Sprague Dawley rats, 4- and 26-week efruxifermin toxicology
safety.note: Paper states the rats' unchanged sympathetic markers mirror unchanged blood pressure and salivary cortisol in efruxifermin-treated T2D and NASH patients.

safety.quote: The absence of an increase in sympathetic tone in rats mirrors the unchanged salivary cortisol and systemic blood pressure following efruxifermin treatment in humans.

safety.population: 451,099 UK Biobank participants, FGF21 rs838133 A allele (putative reduced FGF21 function)
safety.confidence_note: Open access; abstract read. The paper states its aim is to use the human allele to anticipate adverse and beneficial effects of targeting FGF21, so it was offered as a model for the class.
safety.judgement: Model entry. A natural experiment in reduced FGF21 signalling: carriers have higher blood pressure, so agonism should not raise it, the harm PF-05231023 had shown. No drug in the model (product_in_model false).
safety.model: FGF21 rs838133 and truncating-variant carriers (UK Biobank human genetics)

safety.population: High-fat-diet DIO mice, rhFGF21 0.1-3 mg/kg daily for 2 weeks; FGF21 knockout mice
safety.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Native rhFGF21, not a member drug (product_in_model false); Amgen authors (Stanislaus) overlap with the efruxifermin discovery group.
safety.judgement: Model entry. The newer mouse model that contradicted Wei 2012 on bone; per the brief a model that did better is its own track rather than a correction of the failed one.
safety.model: Diet-induced obese mice given recombinant human FGF21 (bone, Amgen)
safety.note: Two weeks of rhFGF21 in DIO mice improved metabolism without any bone loss by DXA, micro-CT or histomorphometry; FGF21 knockouts had normal bone.
safety.short: No bone loss with rhFGF21 in DIO mice
safety.quote: However, bone loss was not detected in rhFGF21-treated mice by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), micro-CT, and histomorphometric analyses.

safety.magnitude_basis: bone mineral density by DXA: predicted no loss vs no change at 12-16 weeks of pegbelfermin
safety.population: NASH F1-F3 patients at 16 weeks (NCT02413372) and obese T2D patients at 12 weeks (NCT02097277)
safety.confidence_note: Kaufman 2020 sets the DIO-mouse rhFGF21 no-bone-loss result (its ref 27) directly before the pegbelfermin BMD sentence quoted, without a verdict. The same 12-16-week DXA caveats as the mouse-fgf21-gain-of-function track apply: NCT02413372 femoral-neck changes are small and noisy, and 16 weeks is short for bone.
safety.judgement: Prospective: the mouse result (2016) precedes any member-drug BMD datum (2018). Matched in direction (no loss predicted, none seen), so same; one source states the comparison but calls the preclinical picture inconsistent rather than resolved.
safety.model: Diet-induced obese mice given recombinant human FGF21 (bone, Amgen)
safety.note: Kaufman 2020 pairs the DIO-mouse rhFGF21 no-bone-loss finding with unchanged BMD after 12-16 weeks of pegbelfermin in T2D and NASH patients.
safety.quote: No change in mean bone mineral density was observed following 12 weeks or 16 weeks of pegbelfermin treatment.
safety.reason: Predicted no bone loss; none seen
